walkthroughs.body_html:
Pipettes for accurate fixed volumes.

Burettes for variable but accurate.

Measuring cylinders for less accurate volumes.

Bunsen: open air-hole for hot blue flame.

Wear safety goggles; tie back hair.

Tabulate independent, dependent and control variables.

Repeat for reliability; mean of concordant readings.

mcqs.q: Most accurate apparatus for 25 cm^3 of liquid:
At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Hess's Law works because energy always cancels out around any cycle.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Enthalpy is a state function — change depends only on initial and final states, not the route taken.
Hess's Law works because reactions can only happen in one specific direction.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Hess's Law works because reactions can only happen in one specific direction.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
